issues.legal_issue: A statement of the lowest price at which an owner would sell does not, without more, constitute an offer capable of acceptance, and a purchaser’s subsequent offer does not form a contract unless the owner accepts it.
material_facts: The owner’s cable stated that he would not accept less than Rs. 10,000, in response to information about a lower offer.
The purchaser later wrote that he confirmed his own offer of Rs. 10,000; he did not state that he accepted a counter-offer.
The owner’s representative later reported the Rs. 10,000 as an offer and asked the owner whether he could sell.
The owner did not accept the purchaser’s offer and instead accepted another buyer’s higher offer.
The suit sought specific performance of the alleged sale contract, and the appeal challenged a decree awarding compensation for breach of that alleged contract.
issues.conclusion: There was no concluded contract in favour of the purchaser. The appeal was allowed, the judgment and decree awarding compensation were set aside, and the suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A mere statement of the lowest price at which a vendor would sell contains no implied contract to sell at that price; it is not an offer unless the communication objectively indicates willingness to be bound. A purchaser’s response to such a statement is itself an offer, which requires acceptance by the vendor to complete a contract. The Court applied Harvey v. Facey [1893] A.C. 552.

rule.if: specific_performance_appeal and price_only_reply and purchaser_made_fresh_offer and seller_never_accepted

predicates.specific_performance_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree in a suit seeking specific performance of an alleged contract of sale.
predicates.price_only_reply: The owner replied to an inquiry by stating only the lowest price he would accept, without expressly undertaking to sell at that price.
predicates.purchaser_made_fresh_offer: The purchaser subsequently communicated a proposal to buy at that price as the purchaser’s own offer.
predicates.seller_never_accepted: The owner did not accept the purchaser’s subsequent offer.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns specific performance and the owner states only a lowest price, the purchaser makes a fresh offer, and the owner does not accept it, the rule means that no concluded contract exists.
